It plays like a classic adventure: talk to odd characters, collect items and combine them to solve puzzles, with a built-in hint system if you get stuck. It is single-player and relaxed in pace, with plenty of dry humor. The Inner World suits fans of traditional point-and-click games.
2131010:
The Land Beneath Us is a turn-based roguelite dungeon crawler set in Annwn, the underworld of Welsh myth. Each run sends you down through floors of enemies, and you work your way toward seven powerful lords while gathering upgrades called Soul-Tech and swapping between a range of weapons. Every move you make lets enemies move too, so positioning and chaining skill combos are the heart of the combat.

Although it is turn-based, it moves quickly, with short decisions rather than long pauses, so runs feel brisk. It is a single-player game, and since each run changes, it rewards replaying and experimenting with builds. It suits players who like tactical puzzles in combat and the steady progress of a roguelite.
1406850:
This side-scrolling action game is built around Liao Tianding, a Taiwanese folk hero remembered as an outlaw who stole from the wealthy and helped the poor. It is set in Taipei during the early twentieth century, when Taiwan was under Japanese rule, and the bustling streets and markets are drawn in a bold style inspired by comic books and traditional art.

In The Legend of Tianding, combat is fast and combo-driven, with a sash that lets Tianding grab enemy weapons and turn them against their owners, plus light role-playing upgrades. It is a single-player game with a steady difficulty curve and a story told in comic-style panels. The Legend of Tianding suits fans of stylish brawlers and historical settings.
1468380:
The Sundew is a pixel-art point-and-click adventure set in a bleak future. You play Anna Isobe, a police officer with cybernetic implants who has been left behind as the world moves on, and who stumbles into a conspiracy that reaches far beyond her own city. The story travels across several locations and asks you to make decisions that change how events unfold and how the story ends.

It plays like a traditional adventure, with conversations, item puzzles and investigation, at a measured pace suited to reading and exploring. It is a single-player game. The Sundew suits players who enjoy cyberpunk fiction and classic adventures in the style of the 1990s, especially those who like stories with choices that carry weight.
966670:
The Wanderer: Frankenstein's Creature retells Mary Shelley's novel from the point of view of the creature. You wake with no memory and no understanding of the world, and you set out on a journey across a landscape painted in soft watercolor style. As you meet people and react to them, your choices shape the creature's view of humanity and how the story ends.

It is a single-player narrative adventure with simple puzzles and musical sequences rather than combat, and the pace is slow and contemplative. Short in length, it works well in one or two sittings. It suits players who enjoy artistic, story-focused games and anyone curious to see a classic piece of literature from a new angle.
1557700:
This full-motion video adventure takes place in a French village during a pandemic lockdown. You follow a man troubled by strange recurring nightmares, and as he digs into their meaning he begins to suspect that the village he lives in is hiding something. The story is told through live-action footage with real actors, and your decisions guide where the investigation goes.

This single-player game works like an interactive film, so the focus is on watching scenes, picking options and piecing together the mystery rather than on reflexes or puzzles. The pace is slow and atmospheric. The World After suits players who enjoy FMV games, psychological mysteries and stories that unfold like a television drama.
1585440:
They Always Run is a 2D action platformer that mixes science fiction with the Wild West. You play Aiden, a mutant bounty hunter with three arms, who travels between planets chasing dangerous criminals with prices on their heads. His third arm is more than a gimmick: it gives him extra ways to block, grab and strike, and the sword-based combat builds on it as the story progresses.

It is a single-player game that mixes platforming, exploration and close-range fighting at a fairly brisk pace, with some tough encounters along the way. The tone is gritty but not grim, much like a frontier adventure set among the stars. It suits players who enjoy melee-focused action games with a distinct setting.
368430:
Played from a third-person view, Through the Woods takes place in the woods along Norway's western coast. A mother searches for her son, who has gone missing, and the night she spends among the trees draws her into a world of creatures taken from Norse folklore. The story is told largely through her recollections as she pushes deeper into the woods.

It is a single-player game built on atmosphere and tension rather than combat, since you mostly explore, hide and avoid threats with a flashlight in hand. The pace is slow and moody, and it can be finished in a few evenings. Through the Woods suits players who enjoy folk horror and walking-focused adventures.
617480:
Tower of Time is a story-driven role-playing game in which you lead a party of heroes down through a mysterious tower buried beneath the earth. Each floor holds puzzles, secrets and fights, and you upgrade your characters and their gear as you go deeper and learn more about where the tower came from. Its combat runs in real time but allows you to pause or slow it down to give orders.

That slowed combat makes it play like a tactics game, with plenty of thought about positioning and skill timing. It is single-player, and alternate modes offer a lighter role-playing ruleset and permanent death for a different challenge. It suits players who like classic party RPGs with tactical battles.
446800:
Transport Fever is a tycoon game about building a transport company from the age of steam to modern times. Starting in 1850, you lay rail lines, set up road routes and later add ships and aircraft to move passengers and goods between towns and industries. Each connection you build has to earn its keep, and as the decades pass new vehicles become available while older ones wear out.

It is a single-player management game with a calm pace, where most of the challenge lies in planning efficient networks and keeping the books in the black. There are campaign missions as well as a free play mode. Transport Fever suits players who enjoy model trains, logistics puzzles and long, slow-building sessions.
690640:
Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince returns the series to its side-on 2.5D style. Three heroes, Amadeus the wizard, Pontius the knight and Zoya the thief, set out to find a runaway prince whose bad dreams are spilling out into the world. Their journey passes through bright fairytale scenery full of physics puzzles and some combat with shadowy creatures.

Each hero has distinct abilities, and puzzles are solved by switching between them or combining their skills. Trine 4 can be played alone or with up to three friends in online or local split-screen co-op, where solutions often become more inventive. The pace is relaxed and the tone is warm, making it a good pick for couples, families and puzzle fans.
1911360:
Trinity Fusion is a sci-fi action roguelite with Metroidvania-style exploration. The multiverse is falling apart, and you play across three separate realities, each with its own version of the main character and its own style of fighting. Runs take you through dark, changing worlds, and between attempts you can merge traits from these parallel selves to build stronger and stranger combinations of weapons and powers.

Combat is fast and fluid, with dodges and quick attacks, so reflexes matter as much as planning your build. It is a single-player game, and the run-based structure makes it easy to play in short bursts while slowly unlocking new options. It suits fans of games like Dead Cells and Hades.
626610:
TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge is a motorcycle racing game built around the famous Tourist Trophy road race on the Isle of Man. Its centerpiece is the full Snaefell Mountain Course, a lap of more than 37 miles over public roads lined with walls, houses and hedges. Real riders and bikes from the event appear, and a career mode lets you work your way up.

The handling leans toward simulation, so it takes practice to keep a bike stable at high speed on narrow, bumpy roads. It offers single-player racing as well as online multiplayer against other riders. It suits motorcycle fans and racing players who want a serious challenge rather than an arcade experience.
292160:
UFO: Aftermath is a tactical strategy game set after an alien attack has devastated Earth. A strange biological mass is spreading across the planet, and you lead the survivors who try to push it back. On the world map you manage bases, research alien technology and decide where to send your teams. Missions then switch to an isometric 3D view, where your squad fights alien forces.

Battles run in real time but can be paused to give orders, so the pace is thoughtful rather than frantic. It is a single-player game in the tradition of the classic X-COM series. UFO: Aftermath suits strategy fans who enjoy managing a long campaign and planning squad tactics.
289500:
UFO: Aftershock is the sequel to UFO: Aftermath and carries on the story of humanity's fight against alien forces on a changed Earth. It combines a global strategy layer, where you expand territory, build bases, manage resources and research new gear, with tactical missions where your squad takes on hostile groups in detailed isolated maps. Compared with the first game, it adds more depth to both halves.

Combat is real-time with pause, so you can stop the action to plan moves and give orders. It is a single-player game with a long campaign and a fair amount of micromanagement. UFO: Aftershock suits strategy players who enjoy X-COM style games and want a broader campaign than the original.
1096410:
This story-driven game from Draw Distance takes place in the World of Darkness and draws on the fifth edition of the tabletop role-playing game. New York's nights are fought over by two vampire factions, the established Camarilla and the rebellious Anarchs. You choose one of three newly made vampires from different clans and try to find a place in this hostile society.

Vampire: The Masquerade - Coteries of New York plays like a visual novel, with illustrated scenes, plenty of reading and dialogue choices that affect relationships and outcomes. It is single-player, with almost no combat and a slow pace. It suits fans of the tabletop game and players who enjoy dark urban fantasy told through text.
1279630:
Vampire The Masquerade - Shadows of New York is a narrative game set in the World of Darkness. You play a newly turned vampire taken in by the Lasombra clan, a group that tolerates no failure. When a prominent figure in the city's vampire community is found dead, you are handed the case, and the investigation pulls you deeper into the politics of New York's undead.

Like Coteries of New York, it is presented as a visual novel, with illustrated scenes and choices that shape conversations and the ending. It is a single-player game focused on story, mood and dialogue rather than action. It suits players who like noir mysteries, dark fantasy and the Vampire: The Masquerade setting.
365770:
Volume is a stealth game from Bithell Games, whose earlier work includes Thomas Was Alone. It reimagines the Robin Hood story in a near future: Rob Locksley uses a simulation device to stream heists that show people how to steal from the rich and expose a corrupt ruler named Gisborne. Levels are clean, top-down virtual spaces where you dodge patrolling guards and collect gems.

Play is about patterns, sightlines and distractions, and you can retry instantly, so each stage becomes a neat stealth puzzle. It is single-player, and a built-in level editor lets players make and share their own stages. Volume suits players who prefer thoughtful stealth over action, and who like short, replayable levels.
1051410:
Close to interactive fiction in form, this is a narrative game. It follows several modern travelers on journeys around the world, and through their experiences it looks at what they are searching for, what worries them and what they hope to find. You make decisions at many points, shaping the course of each trip and how each character changes.

It is a single-player game that is almost entirely text, supported by illustrations, so Wanderlust Travel Stories plays like a choose-your-path book. There is no combat and no time pressure. Wanderlust Travel Stories suits readers, people who love travel writing and players looking for a calm, thoughtful game to enjoy at their own speed.
395570:
Three dwarven astronauts are the heroes of We Are The Dwarves, a tactical adventure played in real time. In their universe, stars sit inside stone, and the trio head into the depths to find new light for their people. Each dwarf has a distinct role and skill set, and you guide them through hostile caverns full of creatures that punish careless moves.

Combat runs in real time but can be paused or slowed to give orders, so it rewards planning, stealth and careful use of abilities. It is a single-player game with a stiff difficulty level. It suits players who enjoy squad tactics in the style of Commandos or Baldur's Gate and do not mind a challenge.
2296990:
We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a short, standalone entry in the We Were Here series of co-op puzzle games. Two players set out on a voyage together, each seeing different parts of a puzzle, and the only way through is to describe what you see and work out the solution together. The tone is lighter than earlier entries, built around a friendship-testing excursion.

It is strictly a two-player online co-op game with no solo mode, and communication by voice chat is essential. Sessions are brief, so it can be finished in an evening, and puzzles change between rounds for replay. It suits pairs of friends or partners who enjoy escape-room style puzzles and talking things through.
226120:
Weird Worlds: Return to Infinite Space, from the small studio Digital Eel, is a roguelike about exploring space. Each game is a short expedition in a randomly generated part of the galaxy, where you pilot a starship, visit star systems, meet odd alien races, find artifacts and recruit allies, all while racing against a time limit before you must return home. Starship battles break out when encounters turn hostile.

A single game takes roughly half an hour, so it fits short sessions and shows something new each time. It is a single-player game with a light, quirky tone and simple controls. Weird Worlds suits players who like quick space adventures and the replay value of a roguelike.
1342620:
Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Heart of the Forest is a narrative role-playing game set in the Bialowieza Forest, one of Europe's oldest stretches of wild woodland, on the border of Poland and Belarus. You play Maia, a young woman who travels there to look into her family history, and soon discovers ties to Garou, werewolves who guard the natural world, and to a growing rage of her own.

It is a single-player game told mostly through text and illustrations, where your choices and how you manage Maia's emotions shape the story and its endings. It is based on the classic tabletop role-playing game. It suits fans of interactive fiction, folklore and slow, character-focused stories.
301560:
White Night is a survival horror game set in the 1930s, presented in stark black and white. After a car crash on a lonely road, the main character takes refuge in an old mansion and becomes trapped there. Inside, he uncovers the house's dark past, while shadowy ghosts lurk in the dark. Light is your main defense, so matches and lamps are precious.

Puzzles revolve around light and shadow, and the game pairs exploration with tense moments of avoiding threats rather than fighting them. It is a single-player experience with a slow, noir-flavored pace and a strong visual style. White Night suits players who enjoy classic haunted-house horror and a moody, film-noir atmosphere.
2820:
X3: Terran Conflict is a space simulation set in the year 2938, after Earth has finally made contact with the alien races of the X setting. Trade flourishes, but friction and open conflict follow. You start with a single ship and are free to trade goods, take on missions, fight pirates, explore sectors and eventually run fleets and factories across the galaxy.

It is a single-player sandbox with a steep learning curve, where much of the play happens through menus and long-term planning as well as in the cockpit. The pace is slow and open-ended. X3: Terran Conflict suits players who want a detailed space economy and a game they can sink many hours into.
888530:
Yaga is an action role-playing game rooted in Slavic folklore. You play Ivan, a blacksmith with one hand and a talent for bad luck, who is sent on a string of impossible tasks by the tzar. As he travels through villages and forests filled with creatures from old tales, the witch Baba Yaga keeps an eye on his fate. The story is narrated in rhyming verse.

Combat centers on Ivan's hammer and tools he forges himself, and how you treat the people you meet changes how the story plays out. It is a single-player game with a hand-drawn look and shifting levels, so replays vary. Yaga suits players who like action RPGs with folklore and humor.
308420:
Ziggurat is a first-person action roguelike in which you play an apprentice wizard sent into a randomly built dungeon as a final test. Armed with a wand, spellbooks, staffs and alchemy weapons, you fight through rooms full of monsters, collect perks as you level up and face bosses at the end of each floor. Since the layout changes every time, no two runs look the same.

Combat is fast and arcade-like, with lots of dodging and a steady stream of projectiles, and a run can be finished in under an hour. It is a single-player game that rewards learning enemies and trying new builds. Ziggurat suits players who like quick shooters with roguelike progression.
1472560:
I Am Fish is a physics-based adventure from Bossa Studios, the team behind I Am Bread. A group of fish friends are separated and taken from their home, and each one has to find a way back to the ocean. That means rolling a fishbowl through houses and streets, flopping across land and swimming through pipes and rivers, with each fish having its own way of moving.

The controls are deliberately tricky, so much of the fun and frustration comes from steering a fragile creature through obstacles. It is a single-player game with a light, comic tone and levels that can be retried quickly. It suits players who enjoy quirky physics puzzles and slapstick challenges.
518699:
Mortal Kombat 11 Ultimate is the complete edition of NetherRealm Studios' fighting game. It includes the base game, the Aftermath story expansion and both Kombat Packs, bringing the full roster of fighters together in one package. The cinematic story mode continues the series' saga, with the keeper of time, Kronika, rewriting history and pulling characters from different eras into conflict with their own pasts.

Fights are one-on-one, with combos, special moves, gory finishers and a detailed system for customizing each character's gear and abilities. You can play alone through the story and towers or face others in local and online multiplayer. It suits fighting game fans of all levels, from casual players to competitive ones.
1228500:
1428: Shadows over Silesia is a dark fantasy action adventure set in medieval Silesia during a time of religious upheaval, when preachers warned that the end of the world was near. Real historical events form the backdrop, while the story leans into folklore and the supernatural.

The game mixes three styles of play: tricky environmental puzzles, demanding melee fights and sneaking past guards when a straight fight would be a mistake. It is a single-player adventure from Polish studio KUBI Games, a good pick if you like story-driven games with a grim, grounded setting and a bit of everything.
255280:
1954 Alcatraz is a point-and-click adventure from Daedalic Entertainment about a stolen fortune. Joe is serving 40 years on Alcatraz for robbing an armored truck, and he is the only one who knows where the money is hidden. Outside, his wife Christine and his old partners in crime all want to find it first.

You switch between Joe inside the prison and Christine on the streets of 1950s San Francisco, and the choices you make with each of them steer the story toward different endings. The hand-drawn look and noir mood suit players who enjoy classic adventure puzzles and character-driven crime stories.
251570:
7 Days to Die is an open-world zombie survival game that blends first-person shooting, crafting, base building, tower defense and role-playing progression. You scavenge the ruined land of Navezgane for food, water and materials, then dig in to fortify a base before the undead come for you.

Every seventh night a blood moon horde attacks, so each week is a race to prepare traps, walls and weapons. Levels and perks let you specialize, nearly everything in the world can be broken down or built, and you can play alone or with friends online, in co-op or against each other.
717610:
A Case of Distrust is a narrative mystery set in San Francisco in 1924, during Prohibition. You play private investigator Phyllis Cadence Malone, who takes a case that pulls her into a web of suspects, secrets and lies. The striking 2D art uses bold colors and silhouettes in the style of the period.

Detective work is about talking, gathering evidence and catching people out. You question witnesses, collect clues and then confront suspects with the proof that contradicts their stories. It is a single-player, story-first game for anyone who likes period crime fiction and solving a case through careful reasoning.
307570:
A Golden Wake is a point-and-click adventure about the rise and fall of a real estate agent in 1920s Miami. You play Alfie Banks, a young salesman who moves to Florida during the land boom and gets caught up in the deals, schemes and people that built the city.

The story is based on real events and real figures of the era, so it doubles as a look at a fascinating slice of American history. It comes from Francisco González, maker of the Ben Jordan series and Shardlight, and suits players who enjoy classic pixel-art adventures with a strong sense of place.
278360:
A Story About My Uncle is a first-person platforming adventure about a boy searching for his missing uncle. His trail leads to a strange, beautiful world of floating islands and caves, and the whole tale is framed as a bedtime story told by a father to his daughter.

Movement is the heart of the game. A special suit lets you swing from surface to surface with a grappling beam and launch yourself in big leaps, and getting the rhythm of each swing right is hugely satisfying. It is a short single-player game that rewards players who love flowing, momentum-based traversal.
751630:
After the Fall is a virtual reality first-person shooter built around four-player co-op, from Vertigo Games, the studio behind Arizona Sunshine. It is set in a frozen, ruined Los Angeles twenty years after a disaster, where hordes of mutated creatures called Snowbreed roam the streets.

You team up with other players to clear runs through the city, collecting loot and upgrading your weapons back at a hub between missions. There is also a competitive mode for player-versus-player fights. You will need a VR headset to play, and it is at its best with a full squad of friends.
1449200:
AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative is a mystery adventure from Spike Chunsoft and the sequel to AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES. Special agents Mizuki and Ryuki, along with their AI partners Aiba and Tama, investigate the Half Body murders, a bizarre case in which only half of each victim is found.

The story jumps between two timelines years apart. You search crime scenes and question people, then dive into suspects' dreams in timed Somnium sequences where odd dream logic hides the truth. Expect plenty of humor alongside the twists, and a story best enjoyed by players who like long, puzzle-driven mysteries.
549260:
Alwa's Awakening is an 8-bit style action adventure from Elden Pixels. You play Zoe, a heroine armed with a magic staff, who sets out to free the land of Alwa from an evil ruler. The world is one large interconnected map with secrets hidden behind every wall.

The staff gains new powers as you go, letting you summon blocks, bubbles and lightning to solve puzzles and reach new areas. Platforming is precise and the bosses can be tough, but checkpoints are generous. It is a single-player game that captures the feel of classic NES adventures with a modern sense of design.
274310:
Always Sometimes Monsters is a story-driven role-playing game about a broke writer setting out on a road trip across the country to win back the love of their life before that person marries someone else. You start with almost nothing and have to work, borrow and bargain your way along.

There is no combat. Instead the game is about choices, many of them uncomfortable, and how they change your relationships and the lives of the people you meet. Small decisions add up to very different journeys, so it suits players who enjoy moral dilemmas and a grounded, personal story.
934780:
American Fugitive is a top-down open-world crime game set in a small American county in the 1980s. You play Will Riley, framed for his father's murder, who breaks out of jail and has to stay ahead of the police while he hunts down the real killer.

Doing that means taking jobs from the local criminal underworld, from burglaries to getaway drives, and staying out of sight when the heat rises. You can steal cars, change clothes to shake pursuers and choose how violent to be. Free updates have added new content, and it plays as a single-player story.
945360:
Among Us is an online and local party game of teamwork and betrayal for 4 to 15 players, set on a spaceship. Most players are Crewmates trying to finish tasks around the map, while one or more are secret Impostors trying to sabotage the ship and pick everyone off.

When a body is found or an emergency meeting is called, everyone debates who looks suspicious and votes someone out. Bluffing, alibis and quick accusations make every round different, especially with friends on voice chat. Matches are short, the rules are easy to learn and it runs well on modest PCs.
18700:
And Yet It Moves is a puzzle platformer set in a world made of torn paper collage. You run and jump like in any platformer, but you can also rotate the entire world around your character, so a wall can become a floor and a falling rock can become a bridge.

Rotation has physical consequences. Your momentum carries over when the world turns, and objects tumble with gravity, so solving each tricky section means thinking about where everything will fall. It is a short, inventive single-player game that suits players who enjoy clever mechanics more than combat.
505640:
Antihero is a fast-paced digital board game where you run a thieves guild in a gaslit Victorian city. You recruit street urchins, hire thugs, grow a gang and upgrade your guild, all while stealing whatever you can from the townsfolk.

Each match is a tight race for victory points through bribery, blackmail and assassination, and a game usually wraps up in under an hour. There is a single-player campaign that teaches the systems, plus online matches against other players. It suits strategy fans who like quick, cunning board game style turns.
447150:
Ape Out is a wildly intense top-down action game about a gorilla escaping captivity. You smash through guards, grab them as shields and throw them into walls as you crash through each level, all in a bold, colorful art style that looks like an old record sleeve.

The soundtrack is frenetic jazz drumming that reacts to what you do, building with every hit and near miss. Levels are partly randomized, so no two runs look quite the same. It is short, fast and violent, a great fit for players who want a stylish arcade experience they can pick up and replay.
1808500:
ARC Raiders is a multiplayer extraction adventure from Embark Studios, set on a future Earth overrun by a deadly mechanized threat known as ARC. You play a Raider who travels up from an underground settlement to the dangerous surface to scavenge supplies and gear.

Each trip is a gamble. You can explore alone or in a small squad, but the machines are lethal and other Raiders may help you or turn on you for your loot. Make it back to an extraction point and you keep what you found, which feeds crafting and upgrades back home.
2399830:
ARK: Survival Ascended is a ground-up remake of ARK: Survival Evolved built in Unreal Engine 5. You wake up on a mysterious island with nothing and have to gather resources, craft tools and build shelter in a world full of dinosaurs and other prehistoric creatures.

The big draw is taming. You can tame, ride and breed hundreds of creatures and use them to hunt, haul and defend your base. You can play alone, join a tribe with friends, or fight other players on online servers, and the community makes heavy use of mods to keep things fresh.
4974620:
As Long As She Forgot is a first-person psychological horror game. You play Marlene, an 86-year-old woman getting her house ready for a visit from her family. They are coming, they always do, and something about the familiar routine of preparing for them is not quite right.

The horror comes from atmosphere and unease rather than constant jump scares, as ordinary chores in a quiet home start to feel wrong. It is a short single-player indie game, released in October 2026, for players who like slow-burn, story-led horror with an unusual point of view.
244210:
Assetto Corsa is a driving simulator from Italian studio Kunos Simulazioni, known for its realistic handling and physics. Its tracks are laser scanned for accuracy, and its cars range from road cars to classic and modern race machines from many famous manufacturers.

You can race in a career, set up custom events, practice hot laps or go online against other drivers. It works best with a steering wheel and pedals, and a huge modding community has added thousands of extra cars and tracks over the years. It is a favorite of sim racers on a budget.
1919470:
Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is an interactive history of Atari from Digital Eclipse. It walks you through 50 years of video games with interviews with designers and industry figures, documentary footage, design documents and original artwork, laid out as a series of timelines.

Along the way you can play more than 90 games from across Atari's arcade machines, home consoles and computers, plus a handful of new games inspired by the classics. Some games support local multiplayer. It is a must for retro fans and anyone curious about how the early game industry came to be.
894620:
ATONE: Heart of the Elder Tree is a hand-drawn adventure inspired by Norse mythology. You play Estra, a young warrior who travels through Midgard to uncover the truth behind her father's death, while the fate of the Elder Tree hangs in the balance.

The game blends interactive storytelling and dialogue choices with logic puzzles, and its combat is a rhythm game where you hit notes in time with the music to fight. The art and soundtrack carry much of its charm. It is a single-player adventure that suits players who enjoy myth, puzzles and music.
621930:
Attack of the Earthlings is a turn-based tactical stealth game with a strong dose of dark comedy. Humans from a greedy intergalactic energy company called Galactoil have come to drill an alien planet, and you play the aliens who live there, fighting back from below.

You command a monstrous Matriarch and her brood, who ambush workers, eat them and evolve into deadlier forms. Clever positioning, distractions and picking off lone targets matter more than brute force. The single-player story is packed with silly, larger-than-life corporate characters to dispose of.
233310:
Avadon 2: The Corruption is a large indie fantasy role-playing game from Spiderweb Software and the second chapter of the Avadon trilogy. You serve the Black Fortress of Avadon as a spy and warrior, protecting your homeland from its enemies with near unlimited authority.

Combat is turn-based with a party of companions, each with their own skills and personal stories. Your choices about loyalty and power shape how things turn out. Like other Spiderweb games, it favors deep writing and lots of content over flashy graphics, so it suits fans of classic party RPGs.
269670:
BADLAND: Game of the Year Edition is an award-winning side-scrolling action adventure set in a dark, beautiful forest. You guide a small flying creature through levels packed with traps and physics puzzles, gathering power-ups that make you bigger, smaller, faster or split you into many clones.

Getting through often means sacrificing some clones to save others, and the silhouette art style gives every level a moody look. This edition adds a large set of levels plus local multiplayer for up to four players on one screen, along with a level editor. It is easy to pick up and hard to master.
2379780:
Balatro is a poker roguelike deckbuilder. You play poker hands to score enough chips to beat each blind, and between rounds you spend money on Joker cards, planet cards and other upgrades that change the rules in your favor.

The magic is in the combos. Jokers stack and multiply in surprising ways, so a run can snowball into absurd scores if you build smartly. Each run is different, with many decks and stakes to unlock, and you do not need to know poker well to start. It is famously hard to put down.
1086940:
Baldur's Gate 3 is a story-rich, party-based role-playing game from Larian Studios set in the world of Dungeons & Dragons. After a mind flayer infects you with a parasite that could transform you, you gather a band of companions and set out to find a cure.

Combat is turn-based and follows D&D rules, with lots of room for creative tactics using the environment. Choices matter everywhere, from how you treat companions to whole storylines that open or close. You can play solo or with up to four players online, and it has won many Game of the Year awards.
451020:
Battle Chasers: Nightwar is a role-playing game inspired by classic console RPGs and based on the Battle Chasers comics by Joe Madureira. A band of heroes is stranded on a mysterious island and must explore it to find a way home, uncovering its dark secrets along the way.

Battles are turn-based in a classic JRPG style, with a system that lets you build up power to unleash big attacks. Procedurally generated dungeons, crafting, fishing and an overworld full of side content keep things varied. It is a single-player game with striking comic book art.
460790:
Bayonetta is a stylish action game from PlatinumGames, directed by Hideki Kamiya. You play Bayonetta, a witch with guns on her hands and feet, fighting through hordes of angels as she tries to recover her lost memories.

Combat is fast and flashy, built on combos, magic attacks and Witch Time, a slow-motion effect you trigger by dodging at the last moment. Ranks at the end of each fight push you to play with more style. The PC version runs at 60 frames per second at high resolutions, the best way to play this classic.
284160:
BeamNG.drive is a vehicle simulator built on a realistic soft-body physics engine. Every part of every car is simulated, so crashes deform metal, bend frames and break components in a way few other games come close to matching.

You can drive freely on large maps, try scenarios and time trials, or just set up spectacular crashes to see what happens. The game covers everything from compact cars to trucks and buses, and a big modding scene adds many more vehicles and maps. It also supports multiplayer and works well with a steering wheel.
761620:
Beholder 2 is a dark satirical adventure set in a totalitarian state. You play an intern at the central ministry with a whole career ahead of you, and climbing the ladder means filling in paperwork, scheming against coworkers and spying on your own bosses.

Every choice comes with a moral cost. You can serve the state faithfully, quietly help the people it crushes, or gather evidence to expose its corruption. Time pressure and tough decisions lead to many different endings. It suits players who enjoyed the first Beholder or like games about difficult choices.
8870:
BioShock Infinite is a first-person shooter from Irrational Games set in 1912. Booker DeWitt, a former soldier deep in debt, is sent to the floating city of Columbia to rescue Elizabeth, a young woman held there since childhood, and to bring her back.

You fight with guns and Vigors, magical powers that set enemies alight or hurl them through the air, and you zip between areas on Skylines, rails that wind through the sky. Elizabeth helps in combat and can open rips into other worlds. The story is famous for its twists and big ideas.
286480:
Black Mirror III is a gothic point-and-click adventure and the final part of the Black Mirror trilogy. Darren is released on bail after the dramatic events of the second game and returns to the village of Willow Creek, haunted by nightmares and questions about his family's past.

You explore the old castle, the village and the crypts below, solving puzzles and talking to suspicious locals to uncover the curse hanging over his family line. Expect a dark, moody mystery with supernatural elements. It plays best after the earlier games, since it picks up their story.
2358720:
Black Myth: Wukong is an action role-playing game from Game Science rooted in Chinese mythology and the classic novel Journey to the West. You play the Destined One, a monkey warrior on a journey that leads to the truth behind a legend from long ago.

Combat centers on staff fighting with different stances, along with spells and transformations that let you take on the powers of defeated foes. The many boss battles are demanding but fair. With stunning visuals and a rich mythical world, it became one of the biggest single-player releases of 2024.
960090:
Bloons TD 6 is a 3D tower defense game from Ninja Kiwi. Balloons, or Bloons, float along a path, and you place monkey towers to pop them before they reach the end. Each monkey has three upgrade paths, so the same tower can play very differently.

Heroes add special abilities, and there are dozens of maps, game modes and difficulty settings, plus regular events and free updates. You can play solo or with up to three other players in online co-op. It is easy to start and deep enough that fans sink in hundreds of hours.
2406770:
Bodycam is a tactical multiplayer first-person shooter shown through a body-camera view, built in Unreal Engine 5. The photoreal visuals and shaky, lens-distorted camera make every fight look like real footage, and the close-quarters gunfights feel raw and loud.

Modes include Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch and Wingman on realistic maps, where callouts, careful angles and teamwork matter more than run-and-gun play. The game is in Early Access, so features and maps are still being added. It suits players who want a tense, grounded shooter with a unique look.
207690:
Botanicula is a humor-filled point-and-click adventure from Amanita Design, the studio behind Machinarium and Samorost. Five little tree creatures set out to save the last seed of their home tree from evil parasites that are draining it of life.

There is no dialogue. Instead you poke, click and experiment with everything on screen, and almost everything reacts with a funny animation or sound. The puzzles are gentle, and the music by Czech band DVA is a big part of its charm. It is a lovely, relaxed game for all ages.
684410:
Bridge Constructor Portal combines the Bridge Constructor series with Valve's Portal. You are a new employee at the Aperture Science Enrichment Center, building bridges, ramps and slides so a convoy of test vehicles can reach the exit of each test chamber.

Portals, propulsion gel, turrets and other familiar Portal devices complicate every level, and your structures need to hold up under real physics. GLaDOS keeps you company with her trademark dry remarks. It is a single-player puzzle game that suits engineering-minded players and Portal fans alike.
1942280:
Brotato is a top-down arena shooter roguelite where you play a potato wielding up to six weapons at once. Aliens attack in short waves, and you dodge and fight to survive until help arrives, picking up materials from every enemy you defeat.

Between waves you spend those materials on items, weapons and stat upgrades, and dozens of characters each change the rules in fun ways. Runs are quick, builds get wild and there is always something new to unlock. You can play solo or in local co-op with friends.
489260:
Brut@l is a modern take on classic ASCII dungeon crawlers. You choose a hero and descend through a procedurally generated dungeon where the walls, floors and enemies are built from 3D ASCII characters, giving it a look all of its own.

You craft weapons by collecting letters and fight with melee, magic and bows, while managing potions and traps. Death is permanent, so each run is a fresh attempt to reach the bottom. You can explore alone or team up with a friend in local co-op, and there is a dungeon editor too.
501590:
Bulletstorm: Full Clip Edition is a remastered first-person shooter from People Can Fly. Grayson Hunt crash lands on an abandoned resort planet, and his choice between survival and revenge drives a loud, crude and funny campaign.

The combat system rewards creativity. You earn points for Skillshots, inventive kills made by kicking, leashing and slamming enemies into spikes, cacti and hazards, then spend them on upgrades. This edition improves the visuals, includes all extra content and adds a mode starring Duke Nukem. There is online co-op too.
2519060:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III is the direct sequel to Modern Warfare II. Captain Price and Task Force 141 face off against the ultimate threat, the ultranationalist war criminal Vladimir Makarov, in a campaign that mixes classic missions with open-ended combat zones.

Multiplayer brings back all 16 launch maps from the original Modern Warfare 2 alongside new ones, and the Zombies mode moves to a large open-world map built around co-op extraction. It plays well across all modes, from solo campaign to online competitive play with friends.
270850:
Car Mechanic Simulator 2014 lets you own and run your own auto repair shop. Customers bring in their cars with problems, and you diagnose faults, order parts, take components apart and put everything back together to fix them.

Each finished job earns money and experience, which you use to expand your garage and unlock new tools and services, from tire changes to engine work. You can also buy wrecks, restore them and sell them on. It is a calm, detailed single-player sim for anyone curious about how cars work.
220740:
Chaos on Deponia is the second part of the Deponia point-and-click adventure series from Daedalic Entertainment. The selfish, accident-prone Rufus is still trying to escape his junkyard planet, and things get messier when Goal, the woman he loves, ends up split into three different personalities.

You solve puzzles by combining items and talking to the planet's oddball residents, with jokes and slapstick on almost every screen. Hand-drawn art and a big world give it plenty to explore. It works best if you have played the first Deponia, and it is even wackier than its predecessor.
319450:
Chariot is a physics-based platform adventure where a princess and her fiance must give the late king the burial he deserves. The king's ghost is never satisfied, so the pair drag his coffin, which rolls on wheels like a chariot, through underground caves in search of the perfect resting place.

Moving the chariot means pushing, pulling, riding on it and swinging it with ropes across gaps and up slopes. It shines in local co-op with a friend, though you can also play alone. Collecting loot buys upgrades and gadgets, and the bright cartoon style keeps the mood light.
269330:
Chronology is a puzzle platform adventure about time travel and an unlikely friendship. An old inventor wakes up with no memory in a ruined world and teams up with a snail to find out what went wrong.

You can travel between the past and the future at any moment, and the world changes around you, with a young tree becoming a tall platform or a ruin standing whole again. The snail can stop time, freezing objects in place. Combining these two powers is the key to every puzzle in this short, charming single-player game.
949230:
Cities: Skylines II is a city-building simulator where you raise a city from the ground up into a thriving metropolis. You lay out roads and zones, provide power, water and services, and keep traffic flowing as the population grows.

The simulation is deep, with a living economy and citizens whose lives respond to your decisions, so problem solving is part of the fun. Maps are huge, there are many tools for detailed design, and seasons and weather add variety. It is the sequel to one of the most popular city builders on PC.
1470390:
City of Beats is a rhythm-driven action roguelite. You cross a futuristic city skyline, shooting enemies whose attacks and movements all follow the beat of the music, and you play best when you fire and dodge in time with the soundtrack.

Every run brings new weapons, upgrades and loot, so you build a different setup each time. The goal is to reach a flow state where shooting feels like playing an instrument. It is a single-player game for players who like roguelites and rhythm games and want something that combines the two.
1903340:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a turn-based role-playing game from Sandfall Interactive. Each year a being called the Paintress paints a number, and everyone of that age dies. You lead the members of Expedition 33 on a mission to destroy her before she can paint death again.

The world is inspired by Belle Epoque France and full of surreal sights and strange creatures. Combat is turn-based but asks you to dodge, parry and time attacks in real time, which makes fights feel active and tense. It was one of the most praised games of 2025 for its story, music and style.
597170:
Clone Drone in the Danger Zone is a robot voxel slice-em-up. Your mind has been downloaded into a robot gladiator, and you must survive the trials of a sinister arena where any part of your body, and your opponents', can be sliced off in combat.

Swords, bows, hammers and spears each play differently, and losing a leg or arm changes how you fight. Beyond the story mode there are endless challenges, online battle royale and co-op modes, plus a level editor and Steam Workshop support. Its humor and chunky look make it great fun with friends.
397950:
Clustertruck is a chaotic physics-based platformer that plays like a game of the floor is lava on top of speeding trucks. The trucks are driven by terrible drivers, so they swerve, crash, flip and fly through the air while you jump from roof to roof.

Levels are short and frantic, and you unlock abilities like double jumps, slow motion and grappling hooks to help you survive. Every attempt plays out a little differently because of the physics. It is a single-player game from Landfall that is easy to pick up and great for quick bursts of play.
411310:
Codename: Panzers, Phase One is a World War II real-time strategy game where you command tanks, infantry and artillery across three campaigns, playing as German, Allied and Soviet forces. Battles move across Europe as the war unfolds.

Units gain experience and carry over from mission to mission, and hero characters add a personal story to each campaign. Careful positioning, cover and combined arms are the key to winning. It is a classic of the genre for strategy fans, with skirmish and multiplayer options as well as the story.
411320:
Codename: Panzers, Phase Two is a World War II real-time strategy game that continues the series in new theaters of war. You fight in the heat of North Africa, the mountains of Italy and the Balkans, commanding tanks, planes, troops and artillery.

Day and night cycles matter, letting you use darkness for surprise attacks, and experienced units and heroes carry over between missions. Campaigns cover several sides of the conflict, including partisan forces. Along with the story there are skirmish, multiplayer and co-op modes for strategy fans.
1218210:
Coromon is a monster-taming role-playing game from TRAGsoft. You join a research team in the region of Velua and set out to catch and train more than 120 Coromon, explore six diverse biomes and uncover a mystery tied to six powerful Titans.

Battles are turn-based and tactical, with each creature's skills, types and stats mattering. The game offers flexible difficulty settings and optional challenge rules for veterans, plus online battles against other players. It is a full 30-plus hour adventure for fans of classic monster-collecting games.
956030:
Creaks is a puzzle adventure from Amanita Design, makers of Machinarium and Botanicula. When the walls of your room start to shake, you discover a hidden world inhabited by bird-like folk and the Creaks, monstrous creatures that hunt anyone they see.

The trick is that Creaks turn back into harmless furniture whenever light shines on them, so you flip switches, move lamps and lure them into place to get past. The hand-painted art and music give it a dreamlike feel. It is a single-player game with thoughtful puzzles that ramp up gently.
2304440:
Creatures of Ava is an action adventure about saving creatures rather than fighting them. You play Vic, who travels to the planet Ava to help its wildlife, where a life-consuming infection called the Withering is spreading across the land.

Using a special staff, you calm and cleanse infected creatures instead of killing them, then tame them and use their abilities to explore ecosystems and solve puzzles. The colorful world and gentle tone make it welcoming. It is a single-player game for players who like exploration and creature companions.
3321460:
Crimson Desert is an open-world action adventure from Pearl Abyss, the studio behind Black Desert. You follow Kliff on his journey to rebuild the Greymane faction and save the continent of Pywel from a looming threat.

The world stretches from wilderness and cities to ancient ruins and the mysterious Abyss, with fast, physical combat, horseback travel and plenty of discovery along the way. It is a single-player story-driven game that suits players who want big battles and a large world to explore.
294370:
Crowntakers is a turn-based strategy role-playing game set in a medieval fantasy world. At the behest of the crown, you lead a band of mercenaries across a randomly generated map to rescue the kidnapped king and defeat the forces of evil.

Battles take place on hex grids where positioning and each unit's skills matter. Between fights you recruit new allies, buy gear and handle random events. Since the world is generated each time, every campaign plays differently. It is a single-player game that suits fans of tactics and roguelike structure.
1158310:
Crusader Kings III is a grand strategy game from Paradox set in the Middle Ages. You guide a noble dynasty through the generations, and when your ruler dies you continue as their heir, so your house's legacy is what really matters.

Every character has traits, ambitions and relationships, and the game plays like a story generator. You can wage war, but you will also arrange marriages, plot schemes, seduce rivals and manage your court and faith. The map stretches from Ireland to India, and you can play solo or online with friends.
406850:
Crush Your Enemies is a fast real-time strategy game that brings back the joy of classic RTS in short, punchy matches. You lead a barbarian horde, choose unit types, manage resources and take enemy territory with clever formations.

Missions are quick, often just a few minutes, and the comedy writing gives the campaign a cheeky tone. There is also online multiplayer to test your tactics against other players. It suits strategy fans who want the essence of the genre without the long build-up of bigger RTS games.
1091500:
Cyberpunk 2077 is an open-world action role-playing game from CD Projekt Red set in Night City, a dangerous megalopolis obsessed with power, glamor and body modification. You play V, a mercenary chasing a one-of-a-kind implant that holds the key to immortality.

You can build V as a hacker, a gunslinger, a blade fighter or a stealthy infiltrator, using cybernetic upgrades to shape your style. Choices shape the story and its endings, and the city is packed with side jobs. After years of updates and the Phantom Liberty expansion, it is widely seen as one of the best RPGs around.
413410:
Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc is a mystery adventure from Spike Chunsoft. Students at an elite academy find themselves trapped inside and are told by a sinister bear named Monokuma that the only way to leave is to kill a classmate and get away with it.

When a murder happens, you search for clues and talk to your classmates, then face a class trial where you fire their own words back at them to expose lies. Fast minigames keep the trials tense. It is a single-player story full of dark humor and big twists, and the start of a beloved series.
567640:
Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is a mystery adventure from Spike Chunsoft. A new cast of 16 students are kidnapped and imprisoned in a school, where Monokuma forces them into a deadly game in which some will kill, some will die and some will be punished.

You investigate twisted murder cases, gather evidence and take part in class trials, which add new tricks like lying, debate scrums and other fast-paced minigames. The story is known for its shocking twists and dark humor. It stands on its own, so you can start here even if you are new to the series.
1374840:
Dark Deity is a turn-based tactical role-playing game in the style of classic grid-based strategy series. You lead a group of young cadets turned soldiers who become heroes in a quest to restore the land of Terrazael, fractured by broken oaths, war and untamed magic.

Every character can follow several class paths, and support conversations between them build relationships that boost them in battle. Collect artifacts, plan each move carefully and choose how hard you want the challenge to be. It is a single-player game for fans of tactics RPGs with a strong story focus.
374320:
Dark Souls III is an action role-playing game from FromSoftware and the final chapter of the Dark Souls trilogy. In the dying kingdom of Lothric, you play the Ashen One, tasked with returning the Lords of Cinder to their thrones as the world falls into ruin.

Combat is tough and deliberate, built on stamina, timing and learning enemy patterns, with unforgettable boss fights. Bonfires serve as checkpoints, and every death is a lesson. You can summon other players for co-op help or be invaded by them. It is a defining game of the genre and a great place to start the series.
532290:
Dark Train is an award-winning steampunk adventure made of paper. You play Ann 2.35f, a mechanical squid tied to a strange railroad machine, and must deliver a mysterious cargo for D. W. Tagrezbung, a famous inventor who has already died.

The train is your world. You move through its carriages, each a puzzle box full of gears, levers and odd creatures, and use your tentacles to manipulate the machinery. The handcrafted look and haunting atmosphere stand out. It is a short single-player game for players who love unusual art and puzzles.
262060:
Darkest Dungeon is a challenging gothic roguelike role-playing game about the psychological stress of adventuring. You recruit, train and lead teams of flawed heroes into dungeons beneath your family estate, battling monsters in turn-based combat.

Heroes suffer stress as well as wounds, and too much stress can break them with afflictions like paranoia or fear, or occasionally inspire them. Back in the hamlet you heal them, upgrade buildings and decide who to sacrifice for the greater good. It is tough and atmospheric, with a famous narrator.
1868140:
DAVE THE DIVER is a casual single-player adventure that mixes deep-sea exploration with running a sushi restaurant. By day, you dive into the mysterious Blue Hole, catching fish and finding treasure; by night, you serve sushi to customers using what you caught.

Both halves keep growing as you go, with new gear, staff, recipes and areas to explore, plus plenty of minigames and story surprises. The pixel art and quirky characters give it lots of personality. It is relaxed, funny and very hard to stop playing once you get into the daily rhythm.
221100:
DayZ is a multiplayer survival game set in a post-apocalyptic land overrun by an infected population. You spawn with almost nothing and must find food, water, weapons and medical supplies while staying alive in a large, unforgiving open world.

The biggest threat is often other players. You can team up with strangers, go it alone or become a bandit, and when you die you lose everything and start over. Every life tells a different story. It suits players who want a tense, realistic survival sandbox where anything can happen.
381210:
Dead by Daylight is an asymmetrical multiplayer horror game where four Survivors face one Killer. The Survivors try to repair generators and open the exit gates to escape, while the Killer hunts them down and sacrifices them to a dark force called the Entity.

There is a large roster of original and licensed killers and survivors from famous horror films and games, each with their own perks and powers. Matches are tense, quick and different every time, and the game has been updated for years with new chapters. It is best enjoyed with friends.
2511800:
Dead in Antares is a turn-based survival management game with role-playing elements from Ishtar Games, makers of Dead in Vinland. A crew sent on a mission to save humanity crashes on an alien planet, and you must keep them alive while finding a way back home.

You manage hunger, health, morale and relationships, assign daily tasks, build up your camp and send survivors out to explore. Tactical combat comes into play when things turn hostile. Every choice has consequences, so planning matters. It suits players who like story-driven survival with a strategy layer.
252610:
Death Road to Canada is a randomly generated road trip action game. You drive a car full of survivors from Florida to Canada, the last safe place, through a land full of slow-moving zombie swarms.

Along the way you search towns for food, fuel and weapons, recruit odd characters, rescue dogs and handle silly random events, while trying to keep everyone alive. Every run is a new story. The pixel art and humor balance the danger, and you can play with a friend in local co-op.
451570:
Demetrios: The BIG Cynical Adventure is a comedic point-and-click adventure. Bjorn Thonen, a hungover antique dealer in Paris, wakes up to find he has been robbed, and his investigation drags him and his friends into an increasingly ridiculous adventure.

Expect crude jokes, absurd situations and plenty of puzzles to solve by combining items and talking to strange characters. Hidden cookies in each scene can be traded for hints if you get stuck. It is a single-player game for players who like classic adventures with a cheeky, irreverent sense of humor.
610370:
Desperados III is a story-driven tactical stealth game from Mimimi Games set in a brutal Wild West. You lead a band of outlaws led by John Cooper as they take on a ruthless land company, using careful plans to take down enemies.

Each character has unique skills, and the Showdown mode lets you pause time to set up several actions and trigger them all at once. Levels are open, with many ways to reach your goal, and replaying them unlocks badges and challenges. It is a hardcore single-player game for patient strategy fans.
556060:
Detective Gallo is a hand-drawn comic noir point-and-click adventure. The hero is a grumpy, feathered private eye, a rooster detective, who takes on a tricky case full of strange suspects and twisted clues in his bustling city.

The game is entirely hand-illustrated and hand-animated, with a dry sense of humor and puzzles that test both your logic and your patience. You explore locations, talk to bizarre characters and piece together what happened. It is a single-player adventure for fans of classic genre comedies.
1222140:
Detroit: Become Human is a narrative adventure from Quantic Dream set in a near future where androids have become more intelligent than humans. You follow three androids, Kara, Connor and Markus, whose stories cross as tension between people and machines reaches a breaking point.

Every choice you make affects the story, with one of the most intricately branching narratives ever made. Characters can die, relationships can break and whole chapters can play out differently. Flowcharts at the end of each scene show the paths you missed. It suits players who love cinematic, choice-driven stories.
337000:
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is an action role-playing game set in 2029, in a world that despises augmented humans. You play Adam Jensen, a veteran covert operative who works for an anti-terrorist task force while unraveling a worldwide conspiracy.

You can approach almost every situation in several ways, using stealth, hacking, conversation or combat, and your augmentations let you build your playstyle. The main hub is a detailed version of Prague full of side missions. It is a single-player game for fans of immersive, choice-driven action.
979310:
Disjunction is a top-down stealth action role-playing game set in a cyberpunk New York in 2048. Three hardened citizens, a private investigator, a former gang enforcer and a hacker, rise up to uncover a conspiracy threatening the city.

Each character plays differently and has their own skill tree, and you can fight your way through with lethal combat or sneak by unseen. The choices you make affect the story and its endings. Detailed pixel art and a synth soundtrack set the mood. It is a single-player game for stealth fans.
220440:
DmC: Devil May Cry is an action game from Ninja Theory that retells the origin story of Dante against a contemporary backdrop. Dante, a young demon hunter, discovers his true nature and joins a fight against demons who secretly control the human world.

Combat is fast and stylish, letting you swap instantly between angelic and demonic weapons to build combos and keep enemies in the air. Many levels take place in Limbo, a twisted version of the city that reshapes itself around you. It is a single-player game for fans of character action.
322330:
Don't Starve Together is the standalone multiplayer version of Don't Starve, Klei Entertainment's uncompromising wilderness survival game. You and your friends are stranded in a strange, dark world and have to gather, craft, farm and build to survive.

Seasons change, monsters roam, and night is especially deadly without a fire. Each character has their own strengths and quirks, and working together is often the difference between thriving and starving. You can play alone or online with others, and years of free updates have added lots of content.
12640:
Drakensang is a party-based role-playing game built on the rules of The Dark Eye, Germany's most popular pen-and-paper role-playing system. You create a hero and travel through the land of Aventuria, gathering companions and getting drawn into a story involving murders and dragons.

Combat is real-time with pause, letting you give orders to your party, and the game uses many skills and talents from the tabletop rules. Quests and crafting fill a world full of detail. It suits fans of classic party RPGs, especially those curious about The Dark Eye setting.
1334730:
Dread Templar is a fast, hardcore old-school first-person shooter that blends the feel of 90s classics with modern touches. You blast through hordes of demons and fiendish enemies across levels packed with secrets, keys and hidden areas, in the spirit of the games that started the genre.

A big arsenal is backed by dozens of weapon upgrades and skills that you unlock and combine to shape how you fight, and a special power lets you turn the tables when things get desperate. It is a single-player game aimed squarely at fans of boomer shooters who want speed, gore and challenge.
229580:
Dream is a first-person exploration game set inside the subconscious mind of Howard Phillips, a young man whose waking life is dull but whose dreams are lucid and powerful. Each night you explore a new dreamscape shaped by his memories, worries and regrets.

There is no combat. Instead you wander strange, surreal places, solve light puzzles and piece together who Howard is and what has happened to him. The story unfolds slowly through what you find and what he says. It is a relaxed single-player game for players who enjoy atmosphere and introspective storytelling.
4019220:
Dressmaker is a cozy crafting game inspired by real dressmaking. You choose fabrics, cut out pattern pieces and sew them together to create the dresses of your dreams, step by step, just as a real dressmaker would.

It is all about the satisfying process of making something by hand, with no rush and no pressure. You can experiment with colors, patterns and styles to design unique pieces. Released in September 2026, it is a relaxing single-player game for anyone who enjoys creative, hands-on simulations.
1896880:
Dungeons of Dreadrock is a puzzle dungeon adventure in the spirit of 1980s home computer games. You play a young woman who descends into the ancient depths of Dreadrock Mountain to find her lost brother, one level at a time.

Each of the 100 levels is a compact room-sized puzzle full of traps, monsters and secret switches, and you must work out the trick to reach the stairs down. Hints are there if you get stuck. The game won several indie awards and suits players who love bite-sized brain teasers with a retro dungeon feel.
3405690:
EA SPORTS FC 26 is the 2025 edition of EA's football series, featuring thousands of licensed players, clubs and leagues. You can play quick matches, build a squad in Ultimate Team, team up with friends in Clubs, or take charge of a club in Career mode.

This edition adds a 48-team international tournament mode, themed Manager Live Challenges and new international ICONs and Heroes in Player Career. It supports single-player, local and online co-op and online matches against other players. It is the go-to pick for football fans who want the full licensed experience.
4080220:
EA SPORTS FC 27 is the 2026 edition of EA's football series, with licensed players, clubs and leagues from around the world. Its new headline feature is The Grounds, a football playground where street-style play meets the stadium.

EA says community-driven changes aim for more control and more true-to-football gameplay across every mode. The usual favorites return, including Ultimate Team, Career mode, Clubs and quick matches, with single-player, co-op and online play. It is the latest choice for fans who want the newest squads and features.
1245620:
ELDEN RING is an acclaimed fantasy action role-playing game from FromSoftware, with worldbuilding by George R. R. Martin. You play a Tarnished, guided by grace, who sets out across the Lands Between to claim the power of the Elden Ring and become an Elden Lord.

The huge open world is full of hidden dungeons, castles and fearsome bosses, and you can travel on horseback, tackle areas in almost any order and build your character however you like. Combat is tough but flexible, with online co-op and invasions. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion adds a vast new region.
1080020:
Electrician Simulator puts you in the shoes of an electrician learning the basics of the job. You visit customers' homes to install sockets, replace light bulbs, lay wires, repair worn-out equipment and assemble broken appliances, checking your work carefully as you go.

Jobs get more complex as you progress, and you earn money to buy better tools and take on bigger tasks. The game shows how real wiring works in a hands-on way, and mistakes have consequences. It is a calm, detailed single-player sim for players who like learning practical skills through play.
523780:
Emily is Away Too is a story told through a retro instant messenger. In your last year of high school, you chat with two friends, Emily and Evelyn, choosing what to type as relationships grow, change and sometimes fall apart.

You also browse a fake web of the era, watching videos and visiting profiles that affect your conversations. The branching story has multiple endings depending on how you handle things. It is short, nostalgic and surprisingly emotional, perfect for anyone who remembers the days of chatting online after school.
933820:
Endzone - A World Apart is a post-apocalyptic survival city builder. After an ecological disaster, you lead a group of survivors out of underground shelters to build a new civilization in a shattered world.

Your settlement faces constant threats such as radiation, toxic rain, sandstorms and drought, so you must plan carefully for water, food and protection. Expeditions let you explore ruins, and raiders can attack. It is a single-player game that suits fans of city builders who like a strong survival challenge.
1203620:
Enshrouded is a survival action role-playing game from Keen Games that you can play solo or in co-op. A corrupting fog called the Shroud is devouring the kingdom of Embervale, and you rise as one of the Flameborn to push it back.

You explore a handcrafted world full of secrets, fight monsters, craft gear and build anything you like with a detailed voxel building system. Skill trees let you shape your hero, and NPCs can join your base. It supports online co-op with friends, and it suits players who love survival games with real exploration.
1812090:
Escape Academy is a puzzle game where you train to become the ultimate Escapist. You attend a strange school and tackle a series of escape rooms, solving puzzles, hacking servers, meeting the faculty and even brewing the perfect cup of tea.

Each room is a self-contained challenge against the clock, packed with clever puzzles and jokes. You can play alone or team up with a friend in local split-screen or online co-op, where communication is key. Expansions add more rooms. It suits fans of real-life escape rooms and puzzle games.
3932890:
Escape from Tarkov is the original extraction first-person shooter. You prepare for raids into the war-torn city of Tarkov, fight other players and AI Scavs, and try to get out alive with your loot. If you die, you lose what you carried in.

The game is hardcore and realistic, with detailed weapon customization, health systems that track wounds and bleeding, and a hideout to upgrade between raids. Every encounter is tense. It suits players who want a demanding, high-stakes shooter and are willing to learn its systems over time.
227300:
Euro Truck Simulator 2 lets you travel across Europe as a trucker delivering cargo across huge distances. You start by taking jobs for other companies, then buy your own trucks, hire drivers and build a transport business.

With dozens of cities to visit and licensed trucks to customize, the game is relaxing and surprisingly addictive. Map expansions add more countries, and online convoy mode lets you drive with friends. It works with a steering wheel or a controller and is a favorite for unwinding with music or podcasts.
5130120:
Evenicle - Next Fragment Medica is a role-playing game from Alicesoft set in a world where human civilization is threatened by monsters. Only a rare few warriors with forbidden skills can fight back, but they face a deadly condition called the Hero Syndrome.

You play a young doctor who may be the only one able to treat it, and the story follows your efforts to keep the heroes going while dealing with the dangers of the world. It is a single-player game released in November 2026 for fans of Japanese RPGs with an unusual premise.
1128920:
EVERSPACE 2 is a fast-paced single-player spaceship shooter with exploration, loot and role-playing elements. You pilot a ship through a vivid handcrafted open world, fighting pirates and other enemies while following a sci-fi story.

Beyond combat, you mine resources, craft upgrades, complete side jobs and explore planets full of secrets and puzzles. Ships can be customized with different weapons, devices and perks to fit your style. It suits fans of space combat who want an action-packed game with lots of gear to collect.
773370:
Exo One is an interplanetary journey through space and time. After a strange signal, you take control of an alien craft that can change its gravity, rolling down hills, gliding through the air and building speed to cross alien worlds.

It is all about movement and atmosphere. Each planet looks very different, from oceans to storms, and you learn to use slopes and flight to gather momentum. The story is minimal and mysterious. It is a short, relaxing single-player game for players who like beautiful environments and smooth, flowing travel.
237430:
Expeditions: Conquistador is a turn-based role-playing game set in the 16th century, when Spanish explorers reached the Americas. You lead an expedition into the New World, searching for gold, fame and adventure.

You manage your party's supplies, health and morale as you explore, make decisions that affect relations with local people and fight in tactical turn-based battles. Every choice matters and resources are tight. It is a single-player game for fans of tactics and historical settings.
445190:
Expeditions: Viking is a party-based role-playing game set around 790 AD. You are the new chieftain of a small Norse clan, and you lead a band of warriors across the sea to Britain in search of wealth and glory.

Combat is turn-based and tactical, and your choices shape alliances, rivalries and the fate of your people back home. You manage your camp, heal wounds and keep your followers happy. It is a single-player game for players who want a historical RPG with real consequences for their decisions.
427520:
Factorio is a game about building automated factories. You start by mining resources by hand, then set up machines, belts and assemblers to produce items of increasing complexity in an infinite 2D world.

As the factory grows, you design production lines, manage logistics and defend against native creatures that attack polluting factories. The Space Age expansion takes you to new planets. You can play alone or in online co-op. It is famously deep and addictive for anyone who loves planning and problem solving.
397060:
Faeria is a strategy card game with a living board. Instead of only playing cards, you build the battlefield itself by placing land tiles, which changes where creatures can move and what you can summon.

The game includes single-player puzzles and a campaign, plus online matches against other players. Its card collection is designed to be easy to complete, so you can focus on strategy rather than chasing cards. It suits players who like card games but want more positional strategy.
864540:
Fallback is a roguelike action adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world. You lead a rebellion of volunteers equipped with jetpacks through a labyrinthine underground complex, fighting robot minions and masters to reach the surface and bring life back.

Each run is procedurally generated, and you jump, dodge and battle through tight sections while collecting upgrades. Your volunteers can die permanently, so careful play matters. It is a single-player game for players who enjoy challenging roguelikes with fast movement.
377160:
Fallout 4 is an open-world role-playing game from Bethesda Game Studios. You are the sole survivor of Vault 111, emerging into a nuclear wasteland in and around Boston, known as the Commonwealth, in search of your missing son.

You can explore freely, take on quests, join factions and build settlements, crafting weapons and armor as you go. Combat mixes shooting with a targeting system that lets you aim at specific body parts. It won many Game of the Year awards and remains one of the most popular open-world RPGs.
13520:
Far Cry is the original open-world shooter from Crytek. Freelance mariner Jack Carver is stranded on a tropical island after his boat is destroyed, and soon uncovers sinister experiments taking place in the jungle.

The game was known for its wide-open levels and smart AI, letting you approach fights in different ways, from long-range shots to close combat. Vehicles let you travel across land and sea. It is a single-player classic for players who want to see where the series began.
220240:
Far Cry 3 is an open-world shooter set on the Rook Islands. You play Jason Brody, a tourist who must rescue his friends from pirates and the infamous Vaas, while discovering your own capacity for violence.

The islands are full of outposts to capture, animals to hunt and side activities. Crafting and skill trees let you grow from a scared tourist into a skilled fighter. A separate co-op campaign adds more to do with friends. It is one of the most beloved entries in the series.
298110:
Far Cry 4 is an open-world shooter set in Kyrat, a war-torn Himalayan region. You play Ajay Ghale, who returns home to scatter his mother's ashes and gets caught up in a civil war against the self-appointed king Pagan Min.

You can explore mountains and valleys, fight on foot, ride elephants and fly gyrocopters. Outposts, side missions and hunting fill the map, and you can play through the world with a friend in co-op. It suits players who want a big, chaotic open-world shooter.
552520:
Far Cry 5 is an open-world shooter set in Hope County, Montana. You play a new deputy who must fight a fanatical doomsday cult called Project at Eden's Gate and its leader Joseph Seed.

You free territory, recruit allies and animal companions, and take on the cult's lieutenants in any order. The entire campaign can be played in two-player co-op, and Far Cry Arcade adds user-made levels. It is a great pick for players who want an action-packed sandbox with friends.
2300320:
Farming Simulator 25 lets you run your own farm, alone or with friends in multiplayer. You plant, grow and harvest crops, raise animals and manage forestry, using hundreds of licensed machines from real manufacturers.

This edition adds new crops such as rice, new environments including an East Asian setting, and improved visuals. You can build and expand your farm however you like. It suits players who enjoy relaxed, detailed simulation and managing a growing business.
501080:
Fishing: Barents Sea is a commercial fishing simulator. You take the helm of your own fishing boat in the Barents Sea, searching for the best fishing zones and selling your catch.
